## Overview

Tools for customer segmentation using RFM (recency, frequency and monetary) analysis.  

## Installation

```{r gh-installation, eval = FALSE}
# Install rfm from CRAN
install.packages("rfm")

# Or the development version from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("rsquaredacademy/rfm")
```

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(rfm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Usage

**RFM** (recency, frequency, monetary) analysis is a behaviour-based technique used to segment customers by examining their transaction history such as:

- how recently a customer has purchased (recency)
- how often they purchase (frequency)
- how much the customer spends (monetary)

It is based on the marketing axiom that **80% of your business comes from 20% of your customers**. RFM analysis helps to identify customers who are more likely to respond to promotions by segmenting them into various categories.

To calculate the RFM score we need the following info for each customer: 

- a unique customer id 
- date of transaction/order
- transaction/order amount

Automatic bins use right-closed quantile intervals: values equal to a cut point
stay in the lower interval, including ties. The first interval includes the
minimum. Recency scores decrease as days increase; frequency and monetary
scores increase with their values. Custom thresholds remain lower-inclusive.
In 0.5.1, automatic cut points no longer add one, so scores are independent of
currency units and customers near a cut point may change score or segment.

```{r rfm_table_order}
# analysis date
analysis_date <- as.Date('2006-12-31')

# generate rfm score
rfm_result <- rfm_table_order(rfm_data_orders, customer_id, order_date,
revenue, analysis_date)

# rfm score
rfm_result
```

## The six segments

The recommended scheme crosses the recency score with a combined
frequency-monetary score, `fm = round((F + M) / 2)`.

Base R's `round()` rounds halves to even, so the result is deterministic.

The six rules cover all 25 R x FM cells exactly once, so every customer lands in
exactly one segment and there are no `Others`.

| Segment | Rule | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Champions | R 4–5 and FM 4–5 | Reward them: early access, referrals; no discounts needed |
| Loyal | R 3 and FM 4–5, or R 4–5 and FM 3 | Cross-sell, loyalty perks, move them up to Champions |
| New / promising | R 4–5 and FM 1–2 | Onboarding and a second-purchase nudge |
| Needs attention | R 3 and FM 1–3 | A timely reminder and a light offer |
| At risk (high value) | R 1–2 and FM 3–5 | Win-back: personal outreach, the strongest offer |
| Lost / hibernating | R 1–2 and FM 1–2 | Low-cost reactivation, or suppress to save spend |

Build `fm` on the `rfm_table_order()` result and map each pair of scores to a
segment with `case_when()`.

```{r six_segments}
six_levels <- c("Champions", "Loyal", "New / promising", "Needs attention",
                "At risk (high value)", "Lost / hibernating")

six_segments <- rfm_result$rfm %>%
  mutate(
    fm = round((frequency_score + monetary_score) / 2),
    segment = case_when(
      recency_score >= 4 & fm >= 4 ~ "Champions",
      (recency_score == 3 & fm >= 4) | (recency_score >= 4 & fm == 3) ~ "Loyal",
      recency_score >= 4 & fm <= 2 ~ "New / promising",
      recency_score == 3 & fm <= 3 ~ "Needs attention",
      recency_score <= 2 & fm >= 3 ~ "At risk (high value)",
      recency_score <= 2 & fm <= 2 ~ "Lost / hibernating"
    ),
    segment = factor(segment, levels = six_levels)
  )
```

Summarise the customers, orders, revenue and average order value in each
segment.

```{r six_segment_summary}
six_summary <- six_segments %>%
  group_by(segment) %>%
  summarise(
    customers = n(),
    orders = sum(transaction_count),
    revenue = sum(amount),
    median_days = median(recency_days),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    pct_customers = round(100 * customers / sum(customers), 1),
    pct_revenue = round(100 * revenue / sum(revenue), 1),
    revenue_per_customer = round(revenue / customers, 2),
    aov = round(revenue / orders, 2)
  ) %>%
  select(segment, customers, orders, revenue, aov, pct_customers, pct_revenue,
         revenue_per_customer, median_days)

knitr::kable(
  six_summary,
  col.names = c("Segment", "Customers", "Orders", "Revenue", "AOV",
                "% customers", "% revenue", "Revenue per customer",
                "Median days since last order")
)
```

A store-owner reading of the table:

- **Champions** are 202 customers (20.3%) and 31.0% of revenue, 711.39 each.
  Reward them with early access and referrals; no discounts needed.
- **Loyal** are 139 customers (14.0%) and 17.6% of revenue, 588.48 each.
  Cross-sell and move them up to Champions.
- **New / promising** are 144 customers (14.5%) but only 9.0% of revenue, with
  an 83.34 average order. Most have already ordered several times (median 4),
  so treat them as recent, lower-spend buyers: onboard them, then raise the
  basket size or frequency to move them towards Loyal.
- **Needs attention** are 112 customers (11.3%) and 7.7% of revenue, with an
  82.69 average order. A timely reminder and a light offer is enough.
- **At risk (high value)** are 161 customers (16.2%) and 21.4% of revenue,
  615.63 each and the highest average order at 101.76. This is the win-back
  list to call first.
- **Lost / hibernating** are the largest group at 237 customers (23.8%) but only
  13.3% of revenue, 260.47 each. Use low-cost reactivation, or suppress them to
  save spend.

Where the revenue sits:

```{r six_revenue_share, fig.align='center', fig.width=7, fig.height=4, fig.alt="Bar chart of share of revenue by segment: Champions 31.0%, Loyal 17.6%, New / promising 9.0%, Needs attention 7.7%, At risk (high value) 21.4%, Lost / hibernating 13.3%."}
ggplot(six_summary, aes(x = segment, y = pct_revenue)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#3b5bdb") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.1f", pct_revenue), "%")),
            vjust = -0.4, size = 3.2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of revenue (%)",
    title = "Revenue share by segment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 20, hjust = 1))
```

The vignette gives the full readings for each segment.

## Example 2: the standard segments

The classic ten segments are defined on the three separate score boxes, and `rfm_segment()` applies them in order with the first match winning. The ten rules overlap in 58 of the 125 R x F x M score cells, so list order matters: "Potential Loyalist" covers many high-frequency, high-monetary customers because it is listed second with a wide box (R 3–5, F 3–5, M 2–5). Ten cells match no rule at all; customers there become `Others` (none in this data). Each bound below is inclusive on both ends.

```{r standard_segments}
# segment names
segment_names <- c("Champions", "Potential Loyalist", "Loyal Customers",
                   "Promising", "New Customers", "Can't Lose Them",
                   "At Risk", "Need Attention", "About To Sleep", "Lost")

# segment intervals
recency_lower <-   c(5, 3, 2, 3, 4, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1)
recency_upper <-   c(5, 5, 4, 4, 5, 2, 2, 3, 3, 1)
frequency_lower <- c(5, 3, 2, 1, 1, 3, 2, 3, 1, 1)
frequency_upper <- c(5, 5, 4, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, 3, 5)
monetary_lower <-  c(5, 2, 2, 3, 1, 4, 4, 3, 1, 1)
monetary_upper <-  c(5, 5, 4, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 4, 5)

# generate segments
segments <- rfm_segment(rfm_result, segment_names, recency_lower,
recency_upper, frequency_lower, frequency_upper, monetary_lower,
monetary_upper)

segments
```

- [plotly](https://plotly.com/r/)
- [gganimate](https://gganimate.com) 

## Shiny App

`rfm` includes a shiny app for interactive RFM analysis. In the latest release, we have added project management features to allow users to save/clone their projects.
